extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and developers (mathematicians and programmers implementing algebraic structures and methods in GAP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual guidance for defining and querying GAP families, filters, categories, representations, attributes, properties, other filters, and types; aimed at implementing and extending GAP objects and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewFamily(name[, req[, imp[, famfilter]]])
rubrics_metrics.description: NewFamily returns a new family fam with name name. The argument req, if present, is a filter of which fam shall be a subset. If one tries to create an object in fam that does not lie in the filter req, an error message is printed. Also the argument imp, if present, is a filter of which fam shall be a subset. Any object that is created in the family fam will lie automatically in the filter imp. The filter famfilter, if given, specifies a filter that will hold for the family fam (not for objects in fam).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Families are always represented as component objects (see 79.2). This means components can be used to store and access useful information about the family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filters (general definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A filter is a special unary GAP function that returns either true or false, depending on whether or not the argument lies in the set defined by the filter. Presently any filter in GAP is implemented as a function which corresponds to a set of positions in the bitlist which forms part of the type of each GAP object, and returns true iff the bitlist of the type of the argument has the value true at all of these positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filters express aspects of information about a GAP object. The intersection (meet) of two filters is again a filter (use 'filt1 and filt2'). Examples: 'IsList and IsEmpty' returns true for empty lists. A filter not the meet of others is a simple filter; simple filters correspond to positions in the type bitlist. Every filter has a rank (see RankFilter).

rubrics_metrics.name: RankFilter(filt)
rubrics_metrics.description: For simple filters, an incremental rank is defined when the filter is created. For an arbitrary filter, its rank is given by the sum of the incremental ranks of the involved simple filters; in addition to the implied filters, these are also the required filters of attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the purpose of computing the rank, attribute testers are treated as if they implied the requirements of their attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NamesFilter(filt)
rubrics_metrics.description: NamesFilter returns a list of names of the implied simple filters of the filter filt, i.e., all those simple filters imp such that every object in filt also lies in imp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ShowImpliedFilters and the creation functions (NewCategory, NewRepresentation, NewAttribute, NewProperty, NewFilter) for how implications between filters arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: FilterByName(name)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds the filter with name name in the global FILTERS list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to find filters that were created but not bound to a global variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShowImpliedFilters(filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Displays information about the filters that may be implied by filter. It first lists filters unconditionally implied by filter, then implications that require further filters (indicated by '+').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example output shows unconditional implications and 'May imply with' entries listing conditional implications that require additional filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: FiltersType(type) / FiltersObj(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of the filters in the type 'type', or in the type of the object 'object' respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FiltersObj(fail) may return [ <Category "IsBool">, <Representation "IsInternalRep"> ].

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of an object are filters that determine what operations an object admits. An object that lies in a category accepts the requirement that it should have methods for certain operations and perhaps satisfy certain axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: IsList requires methods for Length, IsBound[], and element access. Objects can lie in several categories; mutable objects' categories may change when mutated; immutable objects' categories are fixed. All library categories are created at initialization. Indented listings indicate subcategories.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCategory(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if object is a category, and false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: GAP categories are not categories in the usual mathematical sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: CategoriesOfObject(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of the names of the categories in which object lies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CategoriesOfObject(g) returns many category names for a group g.

rubrics_metrics.name: CategoryByName(name)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the category with name name if it is found, or fail otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewCategory(name, super[, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: NewCategory returns a new category cat that has the name name and is contained in the filter super. This means every object in cat lies automatically also in super (super is an implied filter of cat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If creating a category for group elements, choose super = IsMultiplicativeElementWithInverse or a subcategory. If unknown, use IsObject. Optional rank argument denotes incremental rank (default 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareCategory(name, super[, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the same as NewCategory and then binds the result to the global variable name. The variable must previously be writable and is made read-only by this function.

rubrics_metrics.name: CategoryFamily(cat)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a category cat, CategoryFamily returns the family category of cat. This is a category in which all families lie that know from their creation that all their elements are in the category cat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CategoryFamily is technical and of minor importance; see CategoryCollections for related concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: The representation of an object is a set of filters that determines how an object is actually represented (e.g., sparse vs dense storage). An object in a representation accepts the requirement that certain fields in the data structure be present and have specified meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representations form trees (single inheritance). Objects may belong to several representations forming a chain; two representations are either disjoint or one contains the other. Objects may change representation (e.g., mutable list of characters to string). All representations in the library are created during initialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Representations of Objects
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP distinguishes four essentially different ways to represent objects: IsInternalRep (internal objects like integers and permutations), IsDataObjectRep (objects whose data are accessible only by kernel functions), IsComponentObjectRep, and IsPositionalObjectRep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data for IsInternalRep and IsDataObjectRep cannot be manipulated at GAP level. Subrepresentations of IsComponentObjectRep and IsPositionalObjectRep form trees; examples: IsModulusRep, IsDenseCoeffVectorRep. Important subrepresentation: IsAttributeStoringRep for automatic storing of attribute values.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRepresentation(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if object is a representation, and false otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: RepresentationsOfObject(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of the names of the representations object has.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: RepresentationsOfObject(g) might return [ "IsComponentObjectRep", "IsAttributeStoringRep" ].

rubrics_metrics.name: NewRepresentation(name, super[, slots[, req]])
rubrics_metrics.description: NewRepresentation returns a new representation rep that has the name name and is a subrepresentation of the representation super. Every object in rep lies automatically also in super (super is an implied filter of rep).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each representation is a subrepresentation of exactly one of the four main representations. The optional slots and req arguments are unused (backwards compatibility). The incremental rank of rep is 1. See sections 79.2, 79.3, 81.3 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareRepresentation(name, super[, slots[, req]])
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the same as NewRepresentation and then binds the result to the global variable name. The variable must previously be writable and is made read-only by this function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes of an object describe knowledge about it. An attribute is a unary operation without side-effects. An object may store values of its attributes once they have been computed, and claim that it knows these values. Attribute return values are generally immutable unless declared mutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation affects which attributes are stored. Attribute methods should return immutable values or call MakeImmutable to avoid unnecessary copies. Each method installed for an attribute must require exactly one argument lying in the filter given during NewAttribute, unless installed via InstallOtherMethod. Attributes may have multi-argument methods (return values then not stored in arguments). Properties are attributes whose values are only true/false. Examples: Inverse, One, Order, Size, Centre, DerivedSubgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAttribute(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if object is an attribute, and false otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: KnownAttributesOfObject(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of the names of the attributes whose values are known for object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example output shows attributes known after certain computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewAttribute(name, filter[, "mutable"][, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: NewAttribute returns a new attribute getter with name name that is applicable to objects with the property filter. Contrary to categories and representations, the tester of the new attribute does not imply filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional third/fourth args: integer rank sets incremental rank; 'mutable' (string or boolean true) causes attribute values to be mutable; boolean false makes values immutable. Mutable attribute values are stored as-is when set; user is responsible that they are mutable. Example: ComputedSylowSubgroups stores a mutable list. Default tester rank is 1. Methods not requiring the filter must be installed with InstallOtherMethod.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareAttribute(name, filter[, "mutable"][, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the same as NewAttribute and then binds the result to the global variable name. The variable must previously be writable, and is made read-only. It also binds read-only global variables Hasname and Setname for tester and setter.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAttributeStoringRep(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects in this representation have default methods to get stored values of attributes and—if they are immutable—to store attribute values automatically once they have been computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immutable objects in IsAttributeStoringRep will return the same object for subsequent attribute calls. Mutable objects in this rep are allowed but attribute values are not stored automatically; they may be forced to store via explicit setter (use with care). Example: storing rank or trace for a mutable matrix can lead to incorrect stored values after mutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tester(attr)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an attribute attr, Tester(attr) is a filter that returns true or false depending on whether the value of attr for the object is known. Example: Tester(Size)(obj) is true if Size(obj) is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setter(attr)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an attribute attr, Setter(attr) is called automatically when the attribute value has been computed for an immutable object which does not already have a value stored for attr. Setter(attr) can also be called explicitly to set values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DeclareAttribute/DeclareProperty create Hasattr and Setattr names. Example demonstrates SetSize and that setting an intersection property sets all components true. It is not allowed to set an 'and-filter' intersection to false (error and break into REPL).

rubrics_metrics.name: AttributeValueNotSet(attr, obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the value of attribute attr is already stored for obj, returns this value. Otherwise computes and returns attr(obj) without storing it in obj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to obtain large attribute values once without storing them (e.g., element lists). Normal attribute behaviour stores computed values; storing can be disabled/enabled dynamically per-attribute (DisableAttributeValueStoring / EnableAttributeValueStoring). Disabling storing may cause substantial recomputation since library code often assumes stored values for efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: InfoAttributes (info class)
rubrics_metrics.description: This info class (with InfoWarning) is used for messages about attributes. Messages are shown under certain circumstances at specified levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Messages shown when: EnableAttributeValueStoring is used (level 2); DisableAttributeValueStoring is used (level 3); when trying to assign to non-mutable attribute already set to a different value (level 3); when the test filter for an attribute (HasFOO) is set but no value is assigned (level 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: DisableAttributeValueStoring(attr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disables the usual call of Setter(attr) when a method for attr returns a value. In consequence the values will never be stored for that attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that attr must be an attribute (not a property). Disabling storage affects efficiency and may cause repeated computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EnableAttributeValueStoring(attr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enables the usual call of Setter(attr) when a method for attr returns a value; values may be stored again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has no effect unless DisableAttributeValueStoring has previously been used for attr. Note attr must be an attribute, not a property. Example shows Info messages and KnownAttributesOfObject reflecting stored values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Properties are attributes whose values can only be true or false. A property defines two sets: objects for which the value is known, and objects for which the value is known to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tester(prop) checks whether value is known; prop(obj) true iff Tester(prop)(obj) and prop(obj) is true. For immutable objects a known property value is stored as part of the type. Important domain properties: IsAssociative, IsCommutative, IsAnticommutative, IsLDistributive, IsRDistributive (definitions given).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsProperty(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if object is a property, and false otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: KnownPropertiesOfObject(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of the names of the properties whose values are known for object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: KnownPropertiesOfObject(g) returns many property names for a group g; calling Size(g) can add to the known properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: KnownTruePropertiesOfObject(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list of the names of the properties known to be true for object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates differences between KnownPropertiesOfObject and KnownTruePropertiesOfObject after computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewProperty(name, filter[, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: NewProperty returns a new property prop with name name. The filter describes the involved filters of prop. As with attributes, filter is not implied by prop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional rank denotes incremental rank of the property itself (not of its tester); default is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareProperty(name, filter[, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the same as NewProperty and then binds the result to the global variable name. The variable must previously be writable and is made read-only. It also binds read-only Hasname and Setname for tester and setter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Filters (heuristic filters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filters expressing heuristic knowledge (not mathematical concepts), e.g., CanEasilyTestMembership, CanEasilyComputePcgs. Such filters default to false and can be set to true in certain situations explicitly or via logical implication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These filters are not categories/properties/representations. Their value may change for a given object. They behave like attribute testers in that their true value may be required for certain methods. To change them use logical implications or SetFilterObj / ResetFilterObj.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewFilter(name[, implied][, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: NewFilter returns a simple filter with name name. The optional implied argument, if given, must be a filter meaning that for each object in the new filter, implied will also be set. The default value of the new simple filter for each object is false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new filter is intended to be set/reset manually for existing objects then providing implied will cause trouble; consider NewCategory instead. Optional rank denotes incremental rank (default 1). Resetting the new filter does not reset implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareFilter(name[, implied][, rank])
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the same as NewFilter and then binds the result to the global variable name. The variable must previously be writable and is made read-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetFilterObj(obj, filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: SetFilterObj sets the value of filter (and of all filters implied by filter) for obj to true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting the filter may trigger immediate methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: ResetFilterObj(obj, filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: ResetFilterObj sets the value of filter for obj to false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied filters of filter are not touched. This might create inconsistent situations if applied carelessly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types (concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an object obj, its type is formed from its family and its filters (and optionally defining data). The type is itself an object. Two types are equal iff the families are identical, the filters are equal, and (if present) the defining data are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type equality considers family, filters, and defining data; the defining data component is used only in special situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: TypeObj(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the type of the object obj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The returned type is itself an object representing family+filters+(optional data).

rubrics_metrics.name: DataType(type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accesses the defining data component of the type object (the last part of the type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defining data is of minor importance generally; example use: cosets Ug where type may contain group U as defining data. Two cosets mod U and mod V have same type only if U=V.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewType(family, filter[, data])
rubrics_metrics.description: NewType returns the type given by the family family and the filter filter. Optional third argument data is any object that denotes defining data of the desired type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of NewType usage appear in chapters 79.2, 79.3 and chapter 81.
